title: Check-in turn
description: One turn of a voice check-in. The agent reasons over the full disease context and the interval facts, decides what to ask next, and records what the patient just said. Unlike check_in.schema.json — which is the settled record of a whole call — this constrains a single exchange, and carries the agent's own reasoning so a call can be audited question by question.

reasoning.description: Why this question, now — one sentence. The agent chooses its own line of questioning, so this is the audit trail that replaces a fixed schedule: it must be possible to ask afterwards why any question was asked.

say.description: What the agent says aloud this turn. One question, plus at most a brief acknowledgement of what was just said.

covers.description: Ids from the disease context this question is pursuing — check_in_probes, red_flags, trajectory or monitoring ids — or commitment ids. Empty when the agent is following a thread of its own.

should_end.description: True when the agent judges the call complete, or the patient asks to stop. The caller also enforces a hard turn cap; this is the agent's own judgement, not the only stopping condition.

outcomes.description: Commitments the patient addressed in the utterance just heard. Omit commitments not discussed — silence is not an answer.

patient_words.description: Quoted or closely paraphrased. Their words, never a summary of them.

symptom_mentions.description: Symptoms the patient described, mapped onto the disease context's own vocabulary. The watch_for value is constrained at call time to the union of the context's watch_for phrases, so a symptom the context does not name cannot enter the record — which is what makes the cluster count downstream trustworthy.

watch_for.description: The canonical phrase from the context. Constrained to an enum at call time.

flag_id.description: The red_flag id this phrase belongs to.

questions_for_doctor.description: Things the patient asked that the agent must not answer. Carried into the brief.

unprompted_reports.description: Anything the patient reported that does not map onto the context's vocabulary, in their own words. A wrong match is worse than no match, so unmappable material belongs here rather than forced into symptom_mentions.
